media_refs.alt: A librarian, Hayley S, holding a copy of So old, so young by Grant Ginder in front of their face. Text beneath reads: A poignant look at a group of college friends as their lives converge during five different get-togethers across two decades, and how they struggle with the knowledge that they don't fit together the way they once did.

A librarian, Mike, holds a copy of Scratch moss by David Barnett held up in front of their face. Text beneath reads: I'm loving David Barnett's Gemini series, this sinister tale of a cursed mining town and the deal they have with an old god is unputdownable! Scratch Moss add another unnerving layer to the expanding mythos that ramps up the dread that had me reading it on the bus and now hanging out for the next fix!

A librarian, Sarah, holds a copy of Unreliable Narrator by Araminta Hall in front of their face. Text beneath reads: A gripping, twisty thriller that follows the diary entries of a young woman as she's hired as a live-in assistant to a flamboyant yet reclusive writer, and her desperate search for the truth when the writer uses her experience as fodder for his novel.

A librarian, Eamonn, holds a copy of The Palm House by Gwendoline Riley in front of their face. Text beneath reads: Every new Gwendoline Riley novel is a treat and The Palm House is no exception. These is a loose plot of two friends navigating their way through jobs and relationships in contemporary London, but where Riley always shines is the introspection of her characters. This will be the best prose you read all year.
